blocks.text: Thanks to the inroads capitalism has made into Russia, shopping is less of a chore than it ever used to be. During the Soviet period, when various goods would disappear from the state-owned stores, usually with little or no warning and for no apparent reasons, the foreign community (with its валюта hard currency) nearly always had everything it needed or wanted, thanks to the stores known as Берёзка which were off-limits to Soviet citizens. Today, however, Moscow and St. Petersburg and to a lesser extent the capitals of the Newly Independent States are inundated with stores which sell those same goods openly and at prices which are on a par with those in Western Europe and the US.

Today there are very few things which you will be unable to purchase in Moscow or St. Petersburg. Whether it is a Cadillac Seville or Arrow shirts, you can be pretty certain that somewhere in the city there’s somebody selling just what you need. The big problem today is not whether or not you CAN buy something, but WHERE you’re going to find it in the forest of new stores that has replaced the simple берёзки. (The prices in the dialogues are those of 1994, in the roubles of the day.)

blocks.label: Диалог 1

lines.ru: Какую матрёшку вам показать? Вот эту?
lines.en: Which one do you want me to show you? This one?

lines.ru: Да, пожалуйста, эту. Сколько она стоит?
lines.en: Yes, please, this one. How much is it?

lines.ru: Тридцать пять тысяч рублей. Платите в кассу.

blocks.title: В магазине «Подарки»
blocks.setting: An American is buying a матрёшка wooden nesting doll at «Подарки» “Gifts”.

lines.en: I want to buy a shawl.

lines.ru: Какой платок вам показать? Вот этот?
lines.en: Which one would you like me to show you? This one?

lines.ru: Да, пожалуйста, этот. Сколько он стоит?
lines.en: Yes, please, this one. How much is it?

lines.ru: Семьдесят тысяч рублей. Платите в кассу.

blocks.label: Диалог 2

lines.en: Miss, how much are the apples?

blocks.title: На Центральном рынке
blocks.setting: The American is going to the market.

lines.ru: Молодой человек! Сколько стоит кило апельсинов?
lines.en: Young man! How much is a kilo of oranges?

blocks.label: Диалог 3

lines.ru: Скажите, пожалуйста, у вас есть молоко?
lines.en: Please tell me, do you have any milk?

lines.ru: Утром было, а сейчас уже нет.
lines.en: We had some this morning, but now we’re all out.
How much is the cottage cheese?

blocks.title: В гастрономе
blocks.setting: The American is in a гастроном grocery store, at the dairy counter.

blocks.label: Диалог 4

lines.ru: Скажите, пожалуйста, у вас есть докторская колбаса?
lines.en: Please tell me, do you have “Doctorskaya” sausage?
Yes. How much do you want?
That’s 500 roubles. Pay at the register.

blocks.title: В гастрономе
blocks.setting: The American is now at the deli counter.

lines.ru: Простите, у вас есть белый хлеб?
lines.en: Excuse me. Do you have any white bread?
Of course we do. What kind would you like?
And a loaf of black bread.

lines.ru: Пожалуйста. Две тысячи четыреста рублей. Платите в кассу.
lines.en: Here you go. That’ll be 2,400 roubles. Pay at the register.

blocks.label: Диалог 5

lines.en: I want to buy a samovar.

lines.ru: У нас есть разные самовары. Посмотрите, пожалуйста.
lines.en: We have all different kinds of samovars. Take a look.

lines.ru: Это очень хороший старый тульский самовар.
lines.en: This is a very good old samovar, made in Tula.

lines.ru: Да, он мне нравится! Сколько он стоит?
lines.en: Oh yes, I like it! How much is it?

lines.ru: А самовары можно вывозить из страны?

blocks.title: В комиссионном магазине
blocks.setting: On our last shopping trip we’re going to a комиссионный магазин consignment store or second-hand store, a good place to buy antiques, samovars, lithographs, silver, etc.

lines.ru: я хочу, он хочет, вы хотите
lines.en: I want, he wants, you want
